finalChecklist.title: After Systematic Read
items: Correlate with symptoms, vitals, troponin trend
STEMI/Equiv: activate protocol, target D2B < 90 min
QTc ≥ 500 ms: hold QT meds, replete K⁺ > 4 and Mg²⁺ > 2
Wellens TWI: avoid stress test — urgent cath
Mobitz II or 3° AV block: pacing consultation

drugs.name: 2.5% Dextrose + 0.45% NaCl
drugs.pkpd: Hypotonic (~154 mOsm effective after glucose metabolism). Na⁺ 77, Cl⁻ 77 mEq/L + glucose 25g/L (2.5%). Distributes across ECF and ICF. Provides modest electrolytes and calories.
drugs.mechanism: Maintenance fluid designed to replace insensible losses and provide some sodium + glucose. Not for resuscitation. Glucose content prevents ketosis in NPO patients.
drugs.spectrum: Maintenance hydration (NPO, post-op), individualized pediatric maintenance planning, mild hypernatraemia, uncomplicated post-operative maintenance without major electrolyte disturbance.

dose.standard: Adult maintenance: 1–1.5 mL/kg/h; pediatric maintenance must be individualized carefully; do not assume potassium should be added to the bag unless current labs, urine output, and the clinical plan support supplementation

renalAdj.regimen: Standard maintenance rate; monitor electrolytes Q24h
Reduce rate; monitor Na⁺ and K⁺
Avoid without close monitoring — free water causes dilutional hyponatraemia; restricted fluid balance

sideEffects: Hospital-acquired hyponatraemia (hypotonic maintenance → dilutional hyponatraemia especially in SIADH, post-operative, paediatrics — major safety concern)
monitoring: Serum Na⁺ (Q24h during maintenance — watch for downward trend)
publicNotes: Hypotonic maintenance fluids can cause hospital-acquired hyponatremia, especially post-operatively or in SIADH-prone patients
This entry is for the dextrose-containing product, not plain 0.45% sodium chloride
Use it for maintenance, not for resuscitation

drugs.name: Acetaminophen (Paracetamol)
drugs.pkpd: Analgesic and antipyretic effect without clinically meaningful anti-inflammatory or antiplatelet activity. Primarily hepatic glucuronidation/sulfation with a small CYP2E1 pathway producing NAPQI, which is detoxified by glutathione under usual dosing.
drugs.mechanism: Predominantly central prostaglandin synthesis inhibition with downstream analgesic and antipyretic effects. Lacks the peripheral COX inhibition profile of NSAIDs.
drugs.spectrum: First-line mild to moderate pain and fever control, especially when NSAIDs are a poor fit because of GI, renal, or bleeding risk.

dose.standard: 650 mg PO/IV/PR q6h or 1 g q6–8h PRN; usual adult maximum 4 g/day from ALL sources. Frailty, malnutrition, chronic alcohol use, or liver disease often justify keeping total daily dose ≤3 g/day

renalAdj.regimen: Standard dosing; track the total daily dose from all acetaminophen-containing products
Usual dose generally acceptable; many institutions prefer at least a q6h interval
Use a conservative total daily dose and consider q8h spacing; no routine post-HD supplemental dose

sideEffects: Hepatotoxicity in overdose or repeated cumulative excess dosing
Medication-overlap toxicity when combination products are missed
Rare rash or severe cutaneous reactions (SJS/TEN)
Hypotension with IV formulation, especially in critically ill or volume-depleted patients
monitoring: Total 24-hour acetaminophen exposure from all sources and routes
LFTs if prolonged high-dose use or baseline liver disease
publicNotes: Count all combination products because duplicate acetaminophen exposure is a common preventable toxicity
A strong default analgesic when NSAIDs are undesirable, but it does not replace anti-inflammatory therapy when inflammation is the main problem

drugs.name: Acetylcysteine
drugs.pkpd: Ward-reference summary focused on safety review, renal handling, and monitoring rather than exhaustive prescribing.
drugs.mechanism: See class-specific pharmacology; use this entry as a deterministic bedside safety reminder.
drugs.spectrum: Oral mucolytic for viscous respiratory secretions; acetaminophen poisoning requires a separate antidote regimen.

dose.standard: Oral mucolytic — Actein granules 66.7 mg/g: 3 g (approximately 200 mg acetylcysteine) PO three times daily. Check packet weight: both 1.5 g and 3 g packets exist; one packet is not always one adult dose.
dose.Oral mucolytic · 600 mg tablet: Actein 600 mg effervescent tablet: 1 tablet (600 mg) PO once or twice daily according to the Taiwanese product label. Dissolve in water before drinking. Do not apply this tablet count to other strengths or granules.
dose.IV antidote · 3-bag: Acetaminophen poisoning: 150 mg/kg IV over 1 hour → 50 mg/kg over 4 hours → 100 mg/kg over 16 hours (300 mg/kg over 21 hours). At ≥100 kg, the ACETADOTE table uses 15 g → 5 g → 10 g.
dose.IV antidote · 2-bag alternative: Only for ≥41 kg: 200 mg/kg IV over 4 hours → 100 mg/kg over 16 hours (300 mg/kg over 20 hours). At ≥100 kg: 20 g → 10 g. Comparative efficacy is not established in the label; 3-bag may be preferred with large ingestion or early severe liver injury.
dose.IV preparation and reassessment: Use the injectable product (ACETADOTE 200 mg/mL), diluted per its weight-based volume table; reduce fluid volumes for <40 kg or fluid restriction. Monitor for hypersensitivity. Recheck acetaminophen, AST/ALT and INR before stopping; persistent acetaminophen, rising transaminases or elevated INR may require continued treatment with toxicology guidance.

renalAdj.regimen: No renal dose adjustment for antidote use

sideEffects: Dose- or exposure-related toxicity in vulnerable patients
monitoring: Oral mucolytic: secretion clearance and bronchospasm
IV antidote: acetaminophen, AST/ALT and INR
IV infusion: hypersensitivity and fluid balance
publicNotes: Confirm the exact Actein strength and dosage form. Oral mucolytic products are not injectable; mucolytic doses do not treat acetaminophen poisoning.
The IV regimens below describe the US ACETADOTE label, not Taiwanese product availability or a local order set.

references.text: Actein granules 66.7 mg/g — Taiwanese manufacturer label, license 037598 (adult 3 g three times daily)
Actein effervescent tablets 600 mg — Taiwanese manufacturer label, license 045993
Kuang Tien General Hospital — Actein 600 mg effervescent tablet dosing and formulation
ACETADOTE — US prescribing information, revised July 2025, sections 2.2–2.5 (IV antidote)

drugs.name: Acyclovir
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent antiviral exposure after phosphorylation in infected cells. IV therapy is renally eliminated; hydration, infusion duration, and renal adjustment are central safety controls.
drugs.mechanism: Viral thymidine kinase initiates activation to the triphosphate, which inhibits viral DNA polymerase and terminates DNA-chain elongation.
drugs.spectrum: HSV-1, HSV-2, and varicella-zoster virus. IV therapy is used for severe/disseminated disease, encephalitis, and selected immunocompromised patients.

dose.standard: Severe HSV or HSV encephalitis: commonly 10 mg/kg IV q8h; immunocompromised mucocutaneous HSV: 5 mg/kg IV q8h. Infuse every IV dose over at least 1 h with adequate hydration; duration is indication-specific.
dose.loading: Do not give IV acyclovir as a bolus. Verify weight scalar, renal function, hydration, concentration, and infusion time.

renalAdj.regimen: 100% of indicated IV dose q8h
100% of indicated IV dose q12h
100% of indicated IV dose q24h
50% of indicated IV dose q24h
Use renal-adjusted schedule and administer an additional dose after hemodialysis

sideEffects: Crystal nephropathy and acute kidney injury
Neurotoxicity: confusion, tremor, hallucinations, myoclonus, seizures, or encephalopathy—especially with renal accumulation
Phlebitis or tissue inflammation with high concentration/extravasation
TTP/HUS reported rarely in immunocompromised patients
monitoring: Creatinine/CrCl before and during IV therapy
CBC when prolonged or clinically indicated
publicNotes: IV acyclovir must be infused over at least one hour and accompanied by adequate hydration
New confusion or myoclonus in renal impairment should trigger review for acyclovir accumulation rather than automatic escalation for encephalitis
Use narrative pregnancy/lactation labeling and consider severity of untreated maternal infection

drugs.name: Adenosine
drugs.pkpd: Ultra-short half-life of only a few seconds, so effect depends entirely on a rapid push through the most proximal working IV line, immediately followed by a fast flush — a slow push through a distal line often fails to reach the AV node at an effective concentration.
drugs.mechanism: Transiently activates A1 adenosine receptors at the AV node, briefly blocking conduction and interrupting reentrant circuits that use the AV node as part of the loop.
drugs.spectrum: Acute termination of regular narrow-complex SVT, and diagnostic/therapeutic use in select regular monomorphic wide-complex tachycardia per the ACLS tachycardia algorithm.

dose.standard: First dose 6 mg rapid IV push immediately followed by a rapid saline flush; give a second dose of 12 mg if the rhythm has not converted after 1–2 minutes

renalAdj.regimen: No renal dose adjustment needed

sideEffects: Transient flushing, chest tightness, or dyspnea
Transient high-grade AV block or brief asystole (expected mechanism of action, not a separate complication)
Bronchospasm risk in reactive airway disease
May provoke or unmask atrial fibrillation/flutter
monitoring: Continuous ECG during and immediately after administration
IV line patency and proximity to the heart
publicNotes: Warn the patient beforehand that a brief unpleasant sensation is expected and does not indicate a complication
Only for a regular rhythm — do not give for an irregular tachyarrhythmia

drugs.name: Albumin
drugs.pkpd: Ward-reference summary focused on safety review, renal handling, and monitoring rather than exhaustive prescribing.
drugs.mechanism: See class-specific pharmacology; use this entry as a deterministic bedside safety reminder.
drugs.spectrum: Selected hypovolemia; cirrhotic large-volume paracentesis; spontaneous bacterial peritonitis with antibiotics; established HRS-AKI with a vasoconstrictor.

dose.standard: Hypovolemia, when albumin is selected: ALBUMINEX 5% label starts at 25 g IV (500 mL). Reassess after 15–30 minutes; a further dose depends on the hemodynamic response and volume status. Individualize the infusion rate.
dose.Concentration → volume: 5% = 5 g/100 mL; 20% = 20 g/100 mL; 25% = 25 g/100 mL. A 25 g dose therefore occupies 500 mL, 125 mL or 100 mL, respectively. These are volume conversions, not locally stocked vial sizes.
dose.Large-volume paracentesis: Cirrhosis, >5 L removed: 20% or 25% albumin IV after drainage, 8 g per liter of TOTAL ascites removed (BSG/BASL). Example: 8 L removed → 64 g. KASL 2026 gives a 6–8 g/L range.
dose.Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis: With antibiotics: 20% or 25% albumin 1.5 g/kg IV on day 1, then 1 g/kg on day 3; use estimated dry weight. Benefit is clearest with renal dysfunction or jaundice. BSG/BASL specifies increased/rising creatinine and the first dose within 6 hours; KASL 2026 supports adjunctive use in SBP more broadly.
dose.Established HRS-AKI: 20% or 25% albumin 20–40 g/day IV WITH a vasoconstrictor. Reassess volume status daily; stop albumin immediately if fluid overload or pulmonary edema develops (ADQI/ICA 2024; KASL 2026). This is treatment adjunct dosing, not a diagnostic albumin challenge.
dose.Administration: Confirm the product concentration and hydration status. Slow or stop for circulatory overload; stop for suspected anaphylaxis. Do not dilute albumin with sterile water (hemolysis risk).

renalAdj.regimen: No renal dose adjustment, but volume status and pulmonary edema risk drive safety
Use cautiously and reassess response

sideEffects: Dose- or exposure-related toxicity in vulnerable patients
publicNotes: Albumin is not nutrition replacement; use should be tied to a specific volume, cirrhosis, or procedure-related indication.

references.text: ALBUMINEX 5% — US prescribing information, revised May 2024 (hypovolemia and administration)
KASL 2026 — cirrhosis, ascites and related complications (SBP and HRS-AKI)
ADQI/ICA 2024 — AKI in cirrhosis consensus (HRS-AKI treatment and fluid status)

drugs.name: Albuterol (Salbutamol)
drugs.pkpd: Rapid bronchodilation within minutes after inhaled dosing. Systemic spillover increases with repeated nebulization or high rescue use, bringing tremor, tachycardia, and potassium shift into play.
drugs.mechanism: Selective beta2 agonism relaxes airway smooth muscle and improves bronchospasm.
drugs.spectrum: Rescue bronchodilator for asthma or COPD symptoms, acute bronchospasm, and bronchodilator response trials.

dose.standard: MDI: 1–2 puffs q4–6h PRN. Nebulized rescue dosing commonly uses 2.5 mg per treatment, repeated based on severity and protocol

renalAdj.regimen: No routine renal dose adjustment for inhaled use
Monitor heart rate and potassium more closely when escalation is needed

monitoring: Potassium if repeated high-dose nebulization is used
How often rescue therapy is needed
publicNotes: Frequent rescue albuterol use is a signal to reassess the underlying exacerbation plan, not just a cue to keep repeating bronchodilator doses forever
Nebulizer and inhaler dosing are both common, but good inhaler technique often matters as much as the nominal dose

drugs.name: Alfacalcidol
drugs.pkpd: Rapid hepatic conversion to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D allows activity despite impaired renal 1-alpha hydroxylation. Response and toxicity track calcium/phosphate physiology rather than a fixed creatinine-clearance dose.
drugs.mechanism: Converted in the liver to calcitriol, increasing intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption and suppressing parathyroid-hormone drive.
drugs.spectrum: Specialist, biochemically titrated therapy for disorders of calcium metabolism related to impaired 1-alpha hydroxylation, including renal osteodystrophy and selected hypoparathyroid or osteomalacia/rickets syndromes. It is not interchangeable dose-for-dose with nutritional vitamin D.

dose.standard: Product-label starting doses: adults and children over 20 kg 1 microgram PO daily; older adults 0.5 microgram daily. Titrate by 0.25–0.5 microgram increments to biochemical response. Most adult maintenance doses are 0.25–1 microgram daily, but indication and product formulation matter.
dose.loading: Do not use a routine loading dose. Hypercalcaemia requires stopping therapy until calcium normalizes, then the cited product label advises restarting at a reduced dose (often half the previous dose) with monitoring.

renalAdj.regimen: No conventional CrCl dose reduction: titrate to calcium, phosphate, PTH, alkaline phosphatase, and clinical response.
This is a potential indication, not permission for unmonitored dosing. Check calcium frequently; review phosphate control and the complete CKD-mineral/bone plan.
Contraindicated or stop therapy per product labeling; reassess all calcium and vitamin-D products before restarting.

sideEffects: Renal-function deterioration, including reported acute renal failure
monitoring: Corrected or ionized calcium—weekly during initial titration in the cited label
PTH and alkaline phosphatase as clinically indicated
Concurrent calcium, thiazide, magnesium/aluminium antacid, and other vitamin-D products
Arrhythmia risk if hypercalcaemia occurs with digoxin
publicNotes: Alfacalcidol labeling and available formulations differ by country; verify the local product and specialist indication
Do not treat it as ordinary vitamin D supplementation or duplicate it with another active vitamin-D analogue
Hypercalcaemia is the central preventable toxicity: stop and reassess rather than continuing through a rising calcium
In renal bone disease, calcium and phosphate management must be reviewed together; a normal creatinine-based dose table is not sufficient

drugs.name: Alteplase
drugs.pkpd: Short plasma half-life (a few minutes) but the downstream fibrinolytic and bleeding-risk window persists for hours; both eligibility screening and dosing are time-critical.
drugs.mechanism: Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator that converts plasminogen to plasmin, degrading fibrin and dissolving the occluding thrombus.
drugs.spectrum: Acute ischemic stroke within the eligible time window once hemorrhage is excluded and no contraindication is present. Other approved indications (e.g., massive PE, STEMI) use separate protocol-specific dosing not covered by this entry.

dose.standard: Acute ischemic stroke: 0.9 mg/kg IV, maximum 90 mg total — 10% given as an initial bolus over 1 minute, the remainder infused over 60 minutes

renalAdj.regimen: Dose is weight-based, not renal-based; renal impairment does not itself change the stroke dosing regimen

sideEffects: Intracranial or systemic hemorrhage — the major, defining risk
Angioedema (orolingual), especially with concurrent ACE inhibitor use
monitoring: Neuro checks and BP checks per stroke-unit protocol during and after infusion
Watch for angioedema, especially early in the infusion
Urgent repeat imaging for any unexplained neurologic decline (concern for hemorrhagic transformation)
publicNotes: Eligibility (time window, hemorrhage exclusion, contraindication screen) must be confirmed before the first bolus — this is a stroke-team/protocol decision, not a default ward order
Antiplatelet/anticoagulant therapy is typically held for at least 24 hours after, pending the follow-up scan, per local stroke protocol

references.text: AHA/ASA 2026 Guideline for Early Management of Acute Ischemic Stroke

drugs.name: Amikacin
drugs.pkpd: Concentration-dependent (Cmax/MIC). More stable to aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes than gentamicin → active against many gentamicin-resistant GNRs. Once-daily preferred.
drugs.mechanism: Binds 30S ribosomal subunit → bactericidal. Chemical modifications protect from most aminoglycoside-inactivating enzymes (acetyltransferases, nucleotidyltransferases).
drugs.spectrum: Broad GNR coverage including many MDR strains: Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, gentamicin-resistant Enterobacteriaceae. Used in combination for XDR organisms. NOT anaerobes.

dose.standard: 15–20 mg/kg IV q24h (once-daily extended-interval); peak target 56–64 mg/L
dose.loading: 20 mg/kg IV single loading dose

renalAdj.crcl: Normal or mildly reduced renal function
renalAdj.regimen: Use institutional dosing with peak/trough monitoring; official labeling uses 15 mg/kg/day in divided doses unless a local extended-interval protocol is adopted
Adjust dose and/or interval with serum-level monitoring; official labeling allows prolonged-interval or reduced-dose strategies based on creatinine clearance
Do not use the standard renal tables during dialysis; use pharmacist-guided, modality-specific dosing and level monitoring

monitoring: Trough <5 mg/L (extended-interval) or peak 20–30 mg/L / trough <5 mg/L (traditional BID dosing)
publicNotes: Amikacin is often reserved for gentamicin-resistant gram-negative organisms
Like other aminoglycosides, it needs therapeutic drug monitoring and renal surveillance

references.text: IDSA Guidance on Resistant Gram-Negatives — Tamma et al., CID 2023

drugs.name: Amiodarone
drugs.pkpd: Very long half-life with major tissue accumulation and a huge interaction footprint. Acute IV effects and chronic oral toxicity considerations are different enough that both the immediate rhythm indication and the long-term exit plan matter.
drugs.mechanism: Predominantly potassium-channel blockade with additional sodium-channel, calcium-channel, and beta-blocking effects, prolonging repolarization and suppressing atrial and ventricular arrhythmias.
drugs.spectrum: Atrial fibrillation rhythm or rate-control support in selected patients, ventricular arrhythmias, and difficult inpatient rhythm management when other agents are unsuitable or failing.

dose.standard: Highly indication- and route-specific. IV loading and infusion regimens are protocol-based; oral therapy commonly uses a loading phase followed by a lower maintenance dose

renalAdj.regimen: No renal dose adjustment needed
Dose is not CrCl-based, but interaction review and toxicity surveillance are essential regardless of renal function

monitoring: Pulmonary symptom review for chronic therapy
Major interaction review, especially warfarin and digoxin
publicNotes: Amiodarone often solves the immediate rhythm problem while creating a slower outpatient follow-up problem, so document why it was started and what the planned next step is
Starting or stopping amiodarone changes the handling of several common medications, especially warfarin and digoxin

drugs.name: Amlodipine
drugs.pkpd: Long half-life supports once-daily dosing and smooth BP control. It lowers blood pressure gradually and does not need renal adjustment.
drugs.mechanism: Blocks L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle, producing arterial vasodilation with minimal direct AV nodal effect at usual doses.
drugs.spectrum: Hypertension and chronic angina, especially when a once-daily BP agent with preserved renal tolerance is useful.

dose.standard: Start 2.5–5 mg PO daily; usual maintenance 5–10 mg daily. Frail, elderly, or hepatically impaired patients often start at 2.5 mg

renalAdj.regimen: No renal dose adjustment needed
Standard dosing remains appropriate; monitor edema and blood pressure response rather than changing dose for renal function alone

monitoring: Adherence, because the long half-life can hide missed-dose patterns
publicNotes: Amlodipine edema is from precapillary vasodilation and is not the same thing as volume overload, so reflex loop-diuretic escalation is often the wrong fix
A useful BP option when CKD makes ACEi/ARB titration difficult or when beta-blockers are not desired

drugs.name: Amoxicillin
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent killing. %T>MIC target ≥40%. Oral bioavailability ~90% — PO preferred when possible.
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits PBPs (transpeptidases) → disrupts peptidoglycan cross-linking → bactericidal for susceptible organisms.
drugs.spectrum: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae (non-BLNAR), E. faecalis, oral streptococci, Listeria. NOT Staphylococcus, ESBL-GNRs, Pseudomonas, anaerobes.

dose.standard: 500 mg PO TID × 5–7 d (or 875 mg PO BID)

renalAdj.regimen: Standard dose
250–500 mg q24h; dose after dialysis

sideEffects: Maculopapular rash (especially if concurrent EBV mononucleosis — up to 90%)
publicNotes: Prefer oral dosing when feasible because bioavailability is high
Avoid empiric UTI use when local E. coli resistance is high; check your local antibiogram
High-dose amoxicillin may still cover intermediate penicillin-resistant pneumococcus, but high-level resistance needs an alternative

references.text: IDSA/ATS CAP Guidelines — Mandell et al., CID 2007

drugs.name: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate (Augmentin)
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent (amoxicillin component). %T>MIC ≥40%. Clavulanate enhances spectrum by inhibiting class A β-lactamases.
drugs.mechanism: Amoxicillin inhibits PBPs; clavulanate irreversibly inhibits class A β-lactamases (TEM, SHV — NOT AmpC, MBL, ESBL).
drugs.spectrum: MSSA, MRSA (NO), H. influenzae, oral anaerobes, E. coli (susceptible), and amoxicillin-susceptible E. faecalis. NOT ESBL producers, Pseudomonas, or reliably E. faecium.

dose.standard: 875/125 mg PO BID × 5–7 d

renalAdj.regimen: 250/125 mg q12–24h; dose after dialysis

sideEffects: Hepatotoxicity: cholestatic or hepatocellular (rare, watch with prolonged use)
monitoring: LFTs if course >14 days or prior liver disease
publicNotes: Useful oral step-down option for mild to moderate SSTI, dental infections, and community sinusitis
Take with food to reduce GI side effects

references.text: IDSA SSTI Guidelines — Stevens et al., CID 2014

drugs.name: Amphotericin B (Liposomal)
drugs.pkpd: Concentration-dependent. Rapid post-antifungal effect. Tissue distribution highly variable. Liposomal: preferentially accumulated in RES (liver, spleen) with reduced kidney deposition.
drugs.mechanism: Binds ergosterol in fungal membrane → forms ion channels → membrane depolarization and leakage → fungicidal.
drugs.spectrum: Broadest antifungal spectrum: ALL Candida species, Aspergillus, Cryptococcus (drug of choice + 5-FC for meningitis), Mucorales (drug of choice for mucormycosis), Histoplasma, Coccidioides.

dose.standard: Liposomal (AmBisome): 3–5 mg/kg IV q24h; Mucormycosis: 5–10 mg/kg q24h

renalAdj.regimen: Liposomal: standard dose with close monitoring
Liposomal preferred (much less nephrotoxic than conventional). Reduce dose if SCr rising significantly.
Liposomal: standard dose (not cleared by dialysis). Electrolyte replacement critical.

sideEffects: Nephrotoxicity (liposomal << conventional; dose-dependent; hydrate with 500 mL NS before each dose)
Infusion reactions: fever, rigors, hypotension (premedicate: paracetamol 650 mg + hydrocortisone 50 mg ± diphenhydramine 25 mg 30 min before)
Hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia (aggressive daily supplementation essential)
Anaemia (erythropoietin suppression — transfusion may be needed)
monitoring: SCr and urine output daily during initiation (can plateau with liposomal)
K⁺ and Mg²⁺ daily — replace aggressively (K⁺ 40–80 mEq/day supplementation often needed)
Pre-hydration with 500 mL NS before each dose — reduces nephrotoxicity with conventional form
publicNotes: Liposomal amphotericin is preferred over conventional formulations when nephrotoxicity is a concern
Electrolyte replacement and renal monitoring need to be planned from the start of therapy

references.text: IDSA Candida Guidelines — Pappas et al., CID 2016

drugs.name: Ampicillin
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent killing. %T>MIC ≥40%. Short half-life (1–1.5h) → q4–6h dosing. Biliary and renal elimination.
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits PBPs → disrupts peptidoglycan cross-linking → bactericidal for susceptible organisms.
drugs.spectrum: Enterococcus faecalis (not E. faecium), Listeria monocytogenes, streptococci, some oral anaerobes, susceptible Enterobacteriaceae. NOT Staphylococcus, ESBL producers, Klebsiella, Pseudomonas.

dose.standard: 1–2 g IV q4–6h; Listeria/enterococcal endocarditis: 2 g IV q4h

renalAdj.regimen: Standard dose
q12h; supplement after dialysis

sideEffects: Rash (especially with concurrent EBV — up to 90%)
publicNotes: Ampicillin remains a key IV agent for susceptible Enterococcus and Listeria infections
Remember that cephalosporins do not cover Listeria, so ampicillin matters when that diagnosis is on the table

references.text: IDSA Infective Endocarditis Guidelines — Baddour et al., Circulation 2015

drugs.name: Ampicillin-Sulbactam (Unasyn)
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent killing. %T>MIC ≥40%. Sulbactam has intrinsic antibacterial activity vs. Acinetobacter (binds PBP2 directly).
drugs.mechanism: Ampicillin inhibits PBPs; sulbactam inhibits class A/C β-lactamases + directly targets PBP2 of A. baumannii.
drugs.spectrum: MSSA, streptococci, oral anaerobes, H. influenzae, ampicillin-susceptible E. faecalis, and some A. baumannii activity from sulbactam. NOT MRSA, ESBL producers, Pseudomonas, or reliably E. faecium.

dose.standard: 3 g IV q6h (2 g ampicillin + 1 g sulbactam)
dose.loading: CRAB alternative when sulbactam-durlobactam is unavailable: a specialist high-dose regimen delivering 9 g/day of the sulbactam component (27 g/day combination product) plus another active agent

renalAdj.regimen: 3 g q6h
1.5 g q24h; dose after dialysis

publicNotes: Ampicillin-sulbactam can be useful for mixed oral-anaerobic infections and some Acinetobacter isolates
High-dose sulbactam strategies are specialized and usually need ID or pharmacy support

references.text: IDSA/ATS HAP/VAP Guidelines — Kalil et al., CID 2016

drugs.name: Apixaban (Eliquis)
drugs.pkpd: Predictable oral factor Xa inhibition with onset in a few hours and a half-life around 12 hours. Less renal clearance than some other DOACs, but bleeding risk still rises with frailty, procedures, and concomitant antithrombotics.
drugs.mechanism: Direct, selective, reversible inhibition of free and clot-bound factor Xa, reducing thrombin generation and clot propagation.
drugs.spectrum: Nonvalvular atrial fibrillation stroke prevention, DVT/PE treatment, extended VTE prevention, and selected postoperative prophylaxis.

dose.standard: NVAF: 5 mg PO BID. DVT/PE treatment: 10 mg PO BID for 7 days, then 5 mg PO BID. Extended VTE prevention: 2.5 mg PO BID

renalAdj.regimen: Use the indication-specific standard dose unless another labeled reduction rule applies
No single universal CrCl-based reduction fits all adult indications; review age, weight, serum creatinine, bleeding risk, and local policy carefully
Use specialist or institutional guidance rather than a generic table dose

sideEffects: Bleeding including GI, GU, and intracranial bleeding
Spinal or epidural hematoma around neuraxial procedures
monitoring: Renal function for clinical context and peri-procedural planning
Medication interaction review, especially strong P-gp/CYP3A4 modifiers
publicNotes: Routine INR testing is not useful for apixaban effect monitoring
For atrial fibrillation, the 2.5 mg BID dose is for specific labeled reduction criteria, not simply for any CKD by itself
Temporary holds for procedures should follow both procedural bleeding risk and the thrombotic indication

drugs.name: Aspirin (ASA)
drugs.pkpd: Irreversible platelet COX-1 inhibition lasts for the platelet lifespan. Low antiplatelet doses and higher analgesic doses share the same salicylate biology, but bleeding and GI toxicity rise with exposure.
drugs.mechanism: Irreversibly acetylates cyclooxygenase, suppressing thromboxane A2 in platelets and reducing platelet aggregation. Higher doses also reduce prostaglandin-mediated pain and inflammation.
drugs.spectrum: Secondary ASCVD prevention, ACS protocols, stroke/TIA and PAD antiplatelet therapy, and limited analgesic or antipyretic use at higher doses.

dose.standard: Antiplatelet maintenance: 81–100 mg PO daily. ACS loading commonly uses 162–325 mg chewed once, then 81 mg daily

renalAdj.regimen: No standard renal dose adjustment for low-dose antiplatelet therapy
Avoid high analgesic doses and reassess the antiplatelet indication versus bleeding risk carefully

sideEffects: Tinnitus or salicylism at higher doses
monitoring: Clear indication if combined with anticoagulants or another antiplatelet
publicNotes: For long-term cardiovascular prevention, 81 mg daily is usually the maintenance dose
Chewable or non-enteric aspirin is preferred when rapid ACS antiplatelet effect is needed because enteric-coated tablets are slower

drugs.name: Atorvastatin (Lipitor)
drugs.pkpd: Potent LDL lowering with hepatic CYP3A4 metabolism and a long enough effect for once-daily dosing. Cardiovascular benefit comes from sustained long-term use, not short inpatient exposure alone.
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, reducing hepatic cholesterol synthesis and increasing LDL receptor activity.
drugs.spectrum: ASCVD secondary prevention, primary prevention in high-risk patients, diabetes-related lipid management, and high-intensity statin therapy after ACS or ischemic stroke when indicated.

dose.standard: 10–20 mg PO daily to start for many patients; 40–80 mg daily for high-intensity therapy when tolerated and indicated

renalAdj.regimen: No routine renal dose adjustment needed
Dose is still not CrCl-based, but muscle-toxicity risk is higher so interaction review and symptom monitoring matter more

monitoring: Medication interaction review, especially strong CYP3A4 inhibitors
New muscle symptoms or dark urine
publicNotes: Routine CK checks are not needed in every asymptomatic patient, but new muscle pain or weakness deserves follow-up
High-intensity statin therapy after ACS or ischemic stroke is often appropriate unless a clear contraindication or intolerance exists

drugs.name: Atropine
drugs.pkpd: Rapid IV onset, acting only on vagally-mediated slowing at the SA/AV node — it has limited or unreliable benefit for high-grade infranodal (His-Purkinje) block and no effect on a denervated transplanted heart.
drugs.mechanism: Competitively blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors, removing vagal tone and increasing sinus node automaticity and AV nodal conduction.
drugs.spectrum: First-line drug therapy for symptomatic/unstable bradycardia in the ACLS bradycardia algorithm.

dose.standard: 1 mg IV push; repeat every 3–5 minutes to a maximum total dose of 3 mg

renalAdj.regimen: No renal dose adjustment needed

sideEffects: Dry mouth, urinary retention, blurred vision
Can unmask or worsen myocardial ischemia via increased heart rate and oxygen demand
monitoring: Continuous ECG and heart-rate response after each dose
Escalate promptly to pacing/infusion rather than exceeding the maximum dose without response
publicNotes: Do not delay pacing while repeating atropine in a rhythm pattern (Mobitz II, complete heart block) unlikely to respond to it
Ineffective in a denervated transplanted heart because there is no vagal tone to block

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.pkpd: AUC/MIC-dependent. Long half-life ~68h → 5-day courses effective. High tissue concentration; low serum levels. Immunomodulatory effects (DAD inhibition).
drugs.mechanism: Binds 23S rRNA of 50S ribosomal subunit → inhibits translocation. Bacteriostatic. Additional anti-inflammatory/immunomodulatory effects.
drugs.spectrum: Atypicals: Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, Legionella (add to β-lactam for Legionella). Campylobacter (rising resistance). CAP pathogens: some S. pneumoniae (resistance ~30–40% Taiwan). NOT Staph, most Gram-negatives.

dose.standard: PO: 500 mg day 1, then 250 mg days 2–5; IV: 500 mg q24h × 2–5d

renalAdj.regimen: No dose adjustment needed (biliary excretion)

sideEffects: QT prolongation (significant — check baseline QTc; AVOID with other QT-prolonging drugs)
Hearing loss (high doses or prolonged use)
Drug interactions: warfarin (INR ↑), digoxin, CYP3A4 substrates
monitoring: QTc before therapy (especially with cardiac disease, other QT drugs)
publicNotes: Azithromycin is usually best used for atypical coverage rather than broad monotherapy in serious CAP
Check baseline QT risk and interacting medications before use

references.text: IDSA/ATS CAP Guidelines — Mandell et al., CID 2007

drugs.name: Aztreonam
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent β-lactam killing. Activity is Gram-negative only; renal adjustment is important.
drugs.mechanism: Binds PBP3 in susceptible aerobic Gram-negative bacteria. Stable to many β-lactamases but hydrolyzed by ESBLs/AmpC unless paired with an active inhibitor strategy.
drugs.spectrum: Aerobic Gram-negative rods including susceptible Pseudomonas. No Gram-positive or anaerobic activity. Sometimes used in severe β-lactam allergy workflows or paired with avibactam-containing therapy for selected MBL producers.

dose.standard: 1–2 g IV q8h; severe Pseudomonas or systemic infection may require q6–8h dosing by protocol.

renalAdj.regimen: Use usual dosing
Reduce maintenance dose after loading
Further reduction required; dose after HD when applicable

publicNotes: Aztreonam does not cover Gram-positive organisms or anaerobes, so it is rarely complete empiric therapy by itself
Cross-reactivity with most β-lactams is low, but ceftazidime shares a similar side chain and deserves allergy review

drugs.name: Bisacodyl (Dulcolax)
drugs.pkpd: Onset PO: 6–12h (enteric-coated). Onset PR: 15–60 min. Primarily local action. Minimal systemic absorption (high first-pass effect). Pro-drug converted by gut esterases → active BHPM metabolite.
drugs.mechanism: Colonic bacteria and gut esterases convert bisacodyl to BHPM → activates enteric neurons → stimulates colonic propulsive contractions. Reduces water/electrolyte absorption; secretes water and electrolytes into bowel lumen.
drugs.spectrum: Acute constipation, bowel preparation (before procedures), post-operative constipation, opioid-induced constipation adjunct.

dose.standard: PO: 5–10 mg at bedtime (onset next morning); PR: 10 mg suppository (onset 15–60 min); Bowel prep: 10–20 mg PO evening before + 10 mg PR morning of procedure

renalAdj.regimen: No adjustment needed

sideEffects: Abdominal cramping (common, especially PO — smooth muscle stimulation)
monitoring: Electrolytes (K⁺) with frequent or prolonged use
publicNotes: Avoid taking bisacodyl PO within 1 hour of milk or an antacid because the enteric coating can dissolve too early and worsen cramping
PR suppository preferred when rapid effect is needed (15–60 min vs 6–12h for PO)
Do not chew or crush the enteric-coated tablets

drugs.name: Bisoprolol
drugs.pkpd: Ward-reference summary focused on safety review, renal handling, and monitoring rather than exhaustive prescribing.
drugs.mechanism: See class-specific pharmacology; use this entry as a deterministic bedside safety reminder.
drugs.spectrum: General internal medicine ward reference and medication-lab safety rule support.

dose.standard: Indication-specific oral dosing; titrate to heart rate, blood pressure, and HF/perfusion context.

renalAdj.regimen: Start conservatively and monitor bradycardia/hypotension
Hold or reassess

sideEffects: Dose- or exposure-related toxicity in vulnerable patients
publicNotes: A small beta-blocker dose can become too much when acute illness changes heart rate, blood pressure, or renal handling.

drugs.name: Budesonide-Formoterol (Symbicort)
drugs.pkpd: Combines inhaled corticosteroid anti-inflammatory control with long-acting beta2 bronchodilation. It is a controller inhaler, and regimen details depend on whether it is being used only for maintenance or as part of an ICS-formoterol reliever strategy.
drugs.mechanism: Budesonide reduces airway inflammation; formoterol provides long-acting beta2-mediated bronchodilation with relatively rapid onset for a LABA.
drugs.spectrum: Asthma controller therapy, COPD maintenance in selected patients, and maintenance-and-reliever strategies when the specific regimen supports ICS-formoterol use.

dose.standard: Device- and indication-specific. Common outpatient regimens use 1–2 inhalations twice daily, with rescue use only if the prescribed asthma plan specifically uses an ICS-formoterol reliever strategy

renalAdj.regimen: No routine renal dose adjustment for inhaled use
Dose is not renal-based, but adverse-effect tolerance and inhaler technique should still be reassessed carefully

monitoring: Need for rescue therapy or escalation
Whether the patient’s plan is maintenance-only or maintenance-and-reliever
publicNotes: Do not assume all budesonide-formoterol regimens are interchangeable; maintenance-only use and SMART/MART-style use are not the same instructions
Controller efficacy depends heavily on inhaler technique and adherence, not just that the medication is listed in the chart

drugs.name: Bumetanide
drugs.pkpd: Ward-reference summary focused on safety review, renal handling, and monitoring rather than exhaustive prescribing.
drugs.mechanism: See class-specific pharmacology; use this entry as a deterministic bedside safety reminder.
drugs.spectrum: General internal medicine ward reference and medication-lab safety rule support.

dose.standard: Dose is individualized to volume status and prior loop exposure.

renalAdj.regimen: No fixed adjustment; response-guided dosing with close electrolytes/renal monitoring

sideEffects: Dose- or exposure-related toxicity in vulnerable patients
publicNotes: Loop diuretics can worsen AKI or hypokalemia even when needed for congestion.

drugs.name: Calcium Carbonate
drugs.pkpd: Oral calcium carbonate is about 40% elemental calcium by weight and requires gastric acid for dissolution. Supplement absorption is best when taken with food and when elemental-calcium doses are 500 mg or less at one time.
drugs.mechanism: Neutralizes gastric acid when used as an antacid and supplies calcium for intestinal absorption when used as a supplement or prescribed calcium source.
drugs.spectrum: Product- and indication-specific oral therapy for acid indigestion/heartburn or calcium supplementation. The number printed as calcium carbonate is not the same as elemental calcium; verify the product label and intended indication.

dose.standard: Dose by indication and product strength. Example OTC antacid label (1,000 mg calcium carbonate = 400 mg elemental calcium per chewable tablet): chew 2–3 tablets as symptoms occur; do not exceed 7 tablets in 24 hours or use the maximum dose for more than 2 weeks without medical supervision. For supplementation, prescribe and reconcile by elemental-calcium amount; take calcium carbonate with food and split elemental doses above 500 mg.

renalAdj.regimen: No single kidney-function dosing table applies because use may be antacid, supplement, or phosphate-binding therapy; dose by indication and elemental-calcium exposure.
Avoid unsupervised supplementation. Review corrected or ionized calcium, phosphate, concurrent vitamin-D analogues, and the full CKD-mineral/bone plan.
Hold and reassess indication and total calcium intake rather than escalating by symptoms alone.

sideEffects: Hypercalcaemia with excessive or susceptible-patient exposure
Nephrolithiasis or calcium-related tissue deposition with excessive exposure
Reduced absorption of interacting oral medicines
monitoring: Elemental calcium from all medicines and supplements
Corrected or ionized calcium when clinically indicated
Phosphate and renal function in CKD
Medication timing interactions, including separating levothyroxine by at least 4 hours
publicNotes: Reconcile calcium carbonate by elemental calcium, not tablet milligrams alone; 1,000 mg calcium carbonate provides about 400 mg elemental calcium
Calcium carbonate supplements are absorbed better with food, and smaller elemental-calcium doses are absorbed more efficiently
The cited antacid maximum is product-specific: persistent symptoms or repeated maximum-dose use for more than 2 weeks needs reassessment
Calcium carbonate can bind levothyroxine; administer levothyroxine at least 4 hours apart and review timing for other interacting oral medicines

references.text: DailyMed — Calcium Carbonate 1,000 mg Chewable Antacid Label
NIH Office of Dietary Supplements — Calcium: Health Professional Fact Sheet

publicNotes: In hyperkalemia, calcium stabilizes myocardium but does not lower potassium.

drugs.name: Canagliflozin

drugs.mechanism: See class-specific pharmacology; use this entry as a deterministic bedside safety reminder.
drugs.spectrum: General internal medicine ward reference and medication-lab safety rule support.

renalAdj.regimen: Review eligibility and temporary hold during AKI, dehydration, sepsis, surgery, or poor intake
Hold during ketoacidosis or high-risk fasting states

publicNotes: SGLT2 inhibitors can contribute to euglycemic DKA, especially when intake is poor or acute illness is active.

drugs.name: Carvedilol
drugs.pkpd: Ward-reference summary focused on safety review, renal handling, and monitoring rather than exhaustive prescribing.
drugs.mechanism: See class-specific pharmacology; use this entry as a deterministic bedside safety reminder.
drugs.spectrum: General internal medicine ward reference and medication-lab safety rule support.

dose.standard: Indication-specific oral dosing; titrate to heart rate, blood pressure, and congestion/perfusion status.

renalAdj.regimen: No routine renal adjustment, but hypotension, bradycardia, shock, or decompensated HF should trigger review

sideEffects: Dose- or exposure-related toxicity in vulnerable patients
publicNotes: Beta-blockers are discharge-critical for selected HF/ischemic indications but unsafe to escalate through shock or symptomatic bradycardia.

drugs.name: Caspofungin
drugs.pkpd: Concentration-dependent. AUC/MIC target. Highly protein-bound (97%). Poor CNS penetration and urinary tract distribution — not for cryptococcal meningitis or urinary candidiasis.
drugs.mechanism: Non-competitive inhibitor of β-(1,3)-D-glucan synthase → disrupts fungal cell wall synthesis. Fungicidal vs. Candida; fungistatic vs. Aspergillus.
drugs.spectrum: All Candida species (incl. C. krusei, C. glabrata — inherently echinocandin-susceptible). Aspergillus (salvage/combination). NOT Cryptococcus, Mucorales, Fusarium, Trichosporon.

dose.standard: 70 mg IV day 1 (loading), then 50 mg IV q24h; Hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B): 35 mg q24h
dose.loading: 70 mg IV loading dose

renalAdj.regimen: No dose adjustment needed
Standard dose; not significantly cleared by dialysis

sideEffects: Elevated LFTs (mild, transient — usually clinically insignificant)
Histamine-related infusion reactions (rare: flushing, facial swelling)
Drug interactions: rifampin/phenytoin/carbamazepine → increase caspofungin to 70 mg maintenance; tacrolimus level may drop slightly
publicNotes: Caspofungin is a strong first-line option for candidemia and other invasive candidiasis
Once the organism is identified and susceptible, step-down to fluconazole may be appropriate

references.text: IDSA Candida Guidelines — Pappas et al., CID 2016

drugs.name: Cefazolin
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent killing. %T>MIC ≥40%. Short half-life (1.8h) → q8h dosing required for serious infections.
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits PBPs → bactericidal. Narrower gram-negative coverage vs. later-generation cephalosporins.
drugs.spectrum: MSSA, streptococci, E. coli (susceptible), Klebsiella (susceptible), Proteus mirabilis. NOT MRSA, Pseudomonas, Enterococcus, anaerobes.

dose.standard: 1–2 g IV q8h; surgical prophylaxis: 2 g IV × 1 (30 min before incision)

renalAdj.regimen: 1–2 g q8h
1 g q8h
500 mg–1 g q12h
500 mg–1 g after each dialysis session

publicNotes: Cefazolin is often preferred over antistaphylococcal penicillins for MSSA because of better tolerability
It remains a standard surgical prophylaxis agent for many routine procedures

drugs.name: Cefepime
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent killing. Better outer membrane penetration (zwitterionic structure). Adequate CNS penetration. %T>MIC ≥60–70%.
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits PBPs. Stable to AmpC β-lactamases (vs. Enterobacter, Serratia). Zwitterionic structure improves GNR penetration.
drugs.spectrum: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, AmpC-producing Enterobacteriaceae, streptococci, some Gram+. NOT MRSA, ESBL producers, Enterococcus, anaerobes.

dose.standard: 2 g IV q8h (febrile neutropenia, antipseudomonal)

renalAdj.regimen: 2 g q8h
2 g q12h
2 g q24h
1 g q24h
1 g on day 1, then 500 mg q24h; febrile neutropenia: 1 g q24h. Administer after HD

sideEffects: Neurotoxicity: non-convulsive status epilepticus, encephalopathy, myoclonus (especially in renal failure — most important ADR)
monitoring: Renal function — STRICT dose adjustment mandatory!
Mental status changes / EEG if encephalopathy develops in renal failure
publicNotes: Cefepime neurotoxicity is a major risk in renal impairment, so aggressive dose adjustment matters
It is a reasonable option when antipseudomonal coverage is needed and cefepime susceptibility is confirmed or likely

references.text: IDSA/ATS HAP/VAP Guidelines — Kalil et al., CID 2016

drugs.name: Cefiderocol
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent cephalosporin killing. Iron-transport entry can improve activity against difficult Gram-negative pathogens, but exposure still depends on renal dosing.
drugs.mechanism: Binds extracellular iron and enters Gram-negative bacteria through siderophore transporters, then inhibits PBPs. Stable against many β-lactamases including some carbapenemases.
drugs.spectrum: Susceptible aerobic Gram-negative organisms including CRE, MDR Pseudomonas, Stenotrophomonas, and Acinetobacter in selected contexts. NOT Gram-positive or anaerobic coverage.

dose.standard: 2 g IV q8h by prolonged infusion when renal function is normal; adjust by renal function and dialysis modality.

renalAdj.regimen: Use standard dosing
Dose reduction required
Further dose reduction required
Use labeled severe renal impairment or HD dosing
Higher-frequency dosing may be required when CrCl is high; confirm with ID/pharmacy

publicNotes: Cefiderocol should be tied to organism-level susceptibility and source control review, not used as a generic escalation reflex
Renal function must be rechecked during rapidly changing AKI or recovery because dosing can swing in both directions

drugs.name: Ceftazidime
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent killing. %T>MIC ≥50–70%. Antipseudomonal activity distinguishes it from ceftriaxone. Minimal protein binding → good CNS penetration.
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits PBPs (high affinity for PBP3 of Pseudomonas). Stable to many β-lactamases but NOT AmpC inducers or ESBL.
drugs.spectrum: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, most Enterobacteriaceae (not ESBL/AmpC-inducible). Weak Gram+ activity. NOT MRSA, Enterococcus, anaerobes.

dose.standard: 2 g IV q8h; meningitis/life-threatening: 2 g IV q8h (same dose)

renalAdj.regimen: 2 g q8h
2 g q12h
2 g q24h
1 g q24h
500 mg q24h; supplement after HD

sideEffects: Seizures (very high doses in renal failure)
publicNotes: Ceftazidime remains useful when CNS-penetrating antipseudomonal coverage is needed
Avoid overusing it for AmpC-prone organisms when cefepime or a carbapenem is a better fit

references.text: IDSA/ATS HAP/VAP Guidelines — Kalil et al., CID 2016

drugs.name: Ceftazidime-Avibactam (Avycaz)
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent (ceftazidime component). Avibactam restores activity by inhibiting KPC, OXA-48, AmpC, ESBL (NOT MBL/NDM). Target %T>MIC ≥50%.
drugs.mechanism: Ceftazidime inhibits PBPs; avibactam covalently (reversibly) inhibits class A, C, and some D β-lactamases — key advantage over older BL/BLI combinations.
drugs.spectrum: KPC-producing CRE, ESBL Enterobacteriaceae, AmpC inducers, Pseudomonas aeruginosa (including some MDR). NOT MBL-producing organisms (NDM, VIM, IMP).

dose.standard: 2.5 g (ceftazidime 2g + avibactam 0.5g) IV q8h (2h infusion)

renalAdj.regimen: 2.5 g q8h (2h infusion)
0.94 g q48h; dose after HD

sideEffects: Neurotoxicity (high doses/renal failure — similar to cefepime)
monitoring: Renal function — CRITICAL (strict dose adjustment to prevent neurotoxicity)
Culture susceptibility (KPC vs. MBL — caz-avi NOT effective for MBL/NDM!)
publicNotes: Ceftazidime-avibactam is useful for KPC and some OXA-48 producers but not metallo-beta-lactamases like NDM
Carbapenemase typing matters before use

references.text: IDSA Guidance on Resistant Gram-Negatives — Tamma et al., CID 2023

drugs.name: Ceftolozane-Tazobactam
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent β-lactam killing. Extended or optimized infusion may be considered for severe infections where local protocols support it.
drugs.mechanism: Ceftolozane inhibits PBPs with potent Pseudomonas activity; tazobactam inhibits selected class A β-lactamases but does not reliably cover carbapenemases.
drugs.spectrum: Complicated UTI, complicated intra-abdominal infection with metronidazole, and HAP/VAP due to susceptible Gram-negative organisms including many MDR Pseudomonas isolates. NOT MRSA, VRE, atypicals, or reliable CRE therapy.

dose.standard: Indication-specific IV dosing; HAP/VAP dosing is higher than cUTI/cIAI dosing. Confirm indication, renal function, and local infusion protocol.

renalAdj.regimen: Use indication-specific standard dosing
Dose reduction required
Further dose reduction required
Use labeled dialysis dosing and give after HD when applicable
Use ID/pharmacy dosing based on effluent rate and infection severity

monitoring: Renal function before and during therapy
publicNotes: Reserve for documented or strongly suspected resistant Gram-negative infection where narrower agents are not appropriate
Renal dose review is essential because underdosing severe pneumonia and overdosing renal failure are both clinically important risks

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent killing. Long half-life (~8h) → once-daily dosing. Biliary + renal elimination — no dose adjustment for renal failure alone.
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits PBPs (high affinity for PBP2). High CNS penetration (use 2 g q12h for meningitis).
drugs.spectrum: S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, H. influenzae, most Enterobacteriaceae (not ESBL). NOT Pseudomonas, Enterococcus, MRSA, anaerobes, Listeria.

dose.standard: 1–2 g IV/IM q24h
dose.loading: Meningitis: 2 g IV q12h

renalAdj.regimen: No dose adjustment needed (biliary + renal elimination)
Max 2 g/day (avoid accumulation if dual organ impairment)

sideEffects: Biliary sludge / pseudolithiasis (especially prolonged courses — RUQ pain)
Ceftriaxone-Ca²⁺ precipitates (do NOT co-infuse with calcium solutions)
monitoring: Biliary US if RUQ pain develops
publicNotes: Once-daily dosing and no renal-only dose adjustment make ceftriaxone useful when renal function is fluctuating
Escalate to a carbapenem for confirmed ESBL-producing organisms

references.text: IDSA/ATS CAP Guidelines — Mandell et al., CID 2007

drugs.name: Cefuroxime
drugs.pkpd: Time-dependent killing. %T>MIC ≥40%. Oral form (axetil prodrug) ~52% bioavailability — take with food to improve absorption. IV form widely available.
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits PBPs → bactericidal. Broader Gram-negative coverage than 1st-generation; some β-lactamase stability.
drugs.spectrum: MSSA, streptococci, H. influenzae (incl. β-lactamase producers), M. catarrhalis, community Enterobacteriaceae. NOT MRSA, Pseudomonas, Enterococcus, anaerobes, ESBL.

dose.standard: PO: 500 mg BID × 5–10d (with food); IV: 750 mg–1.5 g q8h

renalAdj.regimen: Standard dose
750 mg IV q12h; PO 250 mg BID
750 mg IV q24h; dose after dialysis

sideEffects: GI: diarrhoea, nausea (axetil prodrug has bitter taste)
monitoring: Take oral form with food (significantly improves absorption)
publicNotes: Oral cefuroxime should be taken with food to improve absorption
It can be a reasonable oral step-down agent when H. influenzae coverage is needed

drugs.name: Celecoxib (Celebrex)
drugs.pkpd: Onset: PO 1h. Peak: 2–3h. Duration: 12h (BID dosing). Highly protein-bound (~97%). Hepatic metabolism via CYP2C9. GI-safer than non-selective NSAIDs (COX-1 sparing).
drugs.mechanism: Selective COX-2 inhibition (inducible, inflammation-related) with sparing of COX-1 (gastric cytoprotection, platelet aggregation) → reduced GI ulceration but NO reduction in CV thrombotic risk vs. non-selective NSAIDs.
drugs.spectrum: Osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, acute musculoskeletal pain, dysmenorrhoea, ankylosing spondylitis. Preferred in patients with high GI risk. No meaningful advantage over tNSAIDs for renal or CV safety.

dose.standard: OA: 200 mg/day as 200 mg once daily or 100 mg BID; RA: 100–200 mg BID; Acute pain/dysmenorrhoea: 400 mg once, then an additional 200 mg if needed on day 1, followed by 200 mg BID PRN; Ankylosing spondylitis: 200 mg/day once daily or divided BID (if no response after 6 weeks, 400 mg/day may be tried)
dose.loading: 400 mg PO loading dose for acute pain/dysmenorrhoea

renalAdj.regimen: Standard
Lowest effective dose; shortest duration; monitor renal function
AVOID — same prostaglandin-dependent renal risk as non-selective NSAIDs

sideEffects: CV risk: increased MI/stroke (class effect — similar or greater than non-selective NSAIDs at high doses; highlighted post-APPROVE and CLASS trials)
GI: less mucosal ulceration (COX-1 sparing) — GI advantage is eliminated when combined with low-dose aspirin
Sulfonamide cross-reactivity: theoretical (celecoxib contains sulfonamide group) — monitor in documented sulfa-allergic patients; clinically rare
monitoring: CV risk reassessment for long-term use
GI symptoms (add PPI if on concurrent aspirin)
publicNotes: Celecoxib can reduce GI toxicity relative to nonselective NSAIDs, but it does not eliminate renal or cardiovascular risk
Its GI advantage shrinks if the patient is also taking aspirin

references.text: PRECISION Trial — Nissen et al., NEJM 2016

drugs.name: Ciprofloxacin
drugs.pkpd: Concentration-dependent (AUC/MIC). Best GNR FQ activity. PO bioavailability ~70–80% (reasonable for oral antipseudomonal therapy).
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV → bactericidal. Best among FQs for Gram-negative organisms.
drugs.spectrum: GNRs: Pseudomonas aeruginosa (oral option), E. coli, Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, Haemophilus. Weak S. pneumoniae coverage (NOT for respiratory infections).

dose.standard: 500–750 mg PO BID or 400 mg IV q8–12h (Pseudomonas: 750 mg PO BID or 400 mg IV q8h)

renalAdj.regimen: Standard dose
250–500 mg q24h; administer after dialysis

sideEffects: Drug interactions: warfarin (INR ↑), theophylline, divalent cations reduce oral absorption
monitoring: Take on empty stomach (divalent cations — Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Fe²⁺, Al³⁺ — reduce absorption; separate antacids/milk/supplements by 2h)
publicNotes: Ciprofloxacin is mainly useful for gram-negative and antipseudomonal coverage, not for pneumococcal respiratory infection
Separate oral dosing from polyvalent cations because they markedly reduce absorption

references.text: IDSA UTI Guidelines — Gupta et al., CID 2011

drugs.name: Clindamycin
drugs.pkpd: AUC/MIC-dependent. Bacteriostatic (bactericidal at high concentrations vs. some Streptococcus). Excellent oral bioavailability (~90%). Superior bone, abscess, and soft tissue penetration.
drugs.mechanism: Binds 23S rRNA of 50S ribosomal subunit → inhibits translocation. Same binding site as macrolides and linezolid → cross-resistance (MLSb phenotype).
drugs.spectrum: Anaerobes (B. fragilis, Peptostreptococcus, Fusobacterium), Streptococcus pyogenes, MSSA/MRSA (CA-MRSA strains if susceptible), Toxoplasma (+ pyrimethamine). NOT Gram-negative rods, Enterococcus.

dose.standard: 600–900 mg IV q8h or 300–450 mg PO q6–8h; SSTI: 300–450 mg PO TID

renalAdj.regimen: No dose adjustment needed (hepatic metabolism)
Standard dose; not significantly cleared by dialysis

sideEffects: C. difficile colitis (HIGHEST risk among antibiotics — black box warning; discontinue immediately if diarrhoea develops)
monitoring: Diarrhoea monitoring (C. difficile risk — counsel patient at initiation)
D-zone test for inducible MLSb resistance in MRSA — report clindamycin as S only if negative
publicNotes: Clindamycin should only be relied on for MRSA when inducible resistance testing is negative
Its C. difficile risk is high enough that patients should be counseled to report diarrhea early

references.text: IDSA SSTI Guidelines — Stevens et al., CID 2014

drugs.name: Clobetasol Propionate
drugs.pkpd: Very high local glucocorticoid potency. Systemic absorption rises with large surface area, prolonged treatment, occlusion, altered skin barrier, and high total quantity.
drugs.mechanism: Produces anti-inflammatory, antipruritic, and vasoconstrictive effects through topical glucocorticoid activity and suppression of inflammatory mediator production.
drugs.spectrum: Short-course topical treatment of appropriately diagnosed corticosteroid-responsive dermatoses. Vehicle-specific labels differ: cream, ointment, foam, solution, shampoo, spray, and lotion are not automatically interchangeable in site, age, or duration limits.

dose.standard: For the cited 0.05% emollient cream label, apply a thin layer to affected skin twice daily. Limit routine treatment to 2 consecutive weeks and no more than 50 g/week; stop when controlled. Do not use on face, groin, or axillae, and do not occlude unless specifically directed.
dose.loading: No loading dose. Plaque-psoriasis use beyond 2 weeks is formulation- and label-specific; the cited cream permits selected 5%–10% BSA treatment up to 4 weeks but still limits use to 50 g/week and requires weighing HPA-axis risk.

renalAdj.regimen: No renal dose adjustment. Safety depends on potency, site, treated surface area, barrier integrity, occlusion, duration, age, and weekly quantity.

renalAdj.crcl: Large area / prolonged or occluded use
renalAdj.regimen: Treat as increased systemic-exposure risk; reassess diagnosis and consider HPA-axis evaluation or a lower-potency strategy.

sideEffects: Folliculitis, acneiform eruption, hypopigmentation, or perioral dermatitis
Secondary infection or allergic contact dermatitis
Reversible HPA-axis suppression and glucocorticoid insufficiency
Cushing syndrome, hyperglycaemia, or glucosuria with systemic absorption
monitoring: Exact formulation, strength, body site, and indication
Treatment duration and grams used per week
Treated body-surface area and use of occlusion
Skin atrophy, infection, and response by 2 weeks
HPA-axis suppression when exposure is extensive, prolonged, occluded, or otherwise high risk
Pediatric age and susceptibility to systemic toxicity
publicNotes: Clobetasol is super-high potency: document the body site, intended duration, and approximate weekly quantity rather than prescribing “apply as directed” without limits
For the cited cream, do not exceed 2 consecutive weeks or 50 g/week for routine dermatoses; reassess if not improving by 2 weeks
Avoid the face, groin, axillae, atrophic skin, and occlusive dressings unless a formulation-specific specialist plan clearly says otherwise
Do not assume that instructions for one clobetasol vehicle apply to another; verify the exact cream, ointment, scalp, foam, spray, shampoo, or lotion label

references.text: DailyMed — Clobetasol Propionate 0.05% Emollient Cream Prescribing Information

drugs.name: Clonazepam (Rivotril)
drugs.pkpd: Long elimination half-life (typically 30–40 hours) can produce accumulation. Continued exposure can cause physical dependence, and abrupt reduction can trigger dangerous withdrawal.
drugs.mechanism: Positive allosteric modulation of GABA-A receptors increases inhibitory neurotransmission in the central nervous system.
drugs.spectrum: Selected seizure disorders and panic disorder. In hospital, first establish whether an imported home dose is chronic therapy, because continuation, holding, and tapering carry different risks.

dose.standard: Indication-specific. Panic disorder: start 0.25 mg PO BID; usual target 1 mg/day. Seizure disorders: initial adult dose should not exceed 1.5 mg/day in 3 divided doses, then titrate cautiously. Reconcile the established home regimen rather than substituting a generic ward dose.

renalAdj.regimen: No validated CrCl-based adjustment is defined in the label.
Use caution and monitor for accumulation or excess sedation because metabolites are renally excreted; start at the low end in older or frail patients.

sideEffects: Respiratory depression, especially with opioids, alcohol, or other CNS depressants
Abuse, misuse, addiction, and physical dependence
Potentially life-threatening withdrawal, including seizures, after abrupt discontinuation
monitoring: Sedation, respiratory rate, and oxygenation when other CNS depressants are present
Current indication, duration, and verified home dose
Dependence and a gradual taper plan before dose reduction or discontinuation
publicNotes: Concomitant opioid use can cause profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death; reserve the combination, minimize dose and duration, and monitor closely.
Never abruptly stop established clonazepam after continued use. Confirm the last dose and create a gradual, individualized taper if reduction is intended.
Do not interpret “bedtime home medication” as a low-risk PRN: its long half-life can compound delirium and falls during acute illness.

references.text: FDA Drug Safety Communication — Benzodiazepine Boxed Warning

drugs.name: Clopidogrel (Plavix)
drugs.pkpd: Prodrug that requires CYP2C19 activation. Irreversible platelet inhibition builds over several days without loading, but a loading dose produces faster effect when ACS or PCI protocols require it.
drugs.mechanism: Irreversibly blocks the platelet ADP P2Y12 receptor, reducing activation of the GPIIb/IIIa pathway and platelet aggregation.
drugs.spectrum: ACS and DAPT pathways, post-PCI antiplatelet therapy, aspirin-intolerant secondary prevention, and secondary prevention after recent MI, stroke, or PAD.

dose.standard: Maintenance: 75 mg PO daily. ACS/PCI loading commonly uses 300–600 mg PO once, then 75 mg daily with aspirin according to indication

renalAdj.regimen: No standard renal dose adjustment
Use standard dosing but reassess net benefit frequently because both bleeding and thrombotic risk are higher

sideEffects: Reduced antiplatelet effect with poor CYP2C19 activation or interacting drugs
monitoring: Platelet count if thrombocytopenia or TTP is suspected
publicNotes: Avoid omeprazole and esomeprazole when possible because they reduce CYP2C19 activation; pantoprazole is usually the easiest alternative if a PPI is needed
Clopidogrel is commonly paired with aspirin after ACS or PCI, but the duration depends on stent type and bleeding risk

drugs.name: Colistin (Polymyxin E)
drugs.pkpd: Concentration-dependent (AUC/MIC + Cmax/MIC). Colistimethate sodium (CMS) is prodrug → converted to colistin in vivo. PK highly variable — loading dose critical to achieve therapeutic levels quickly.
drugs.mechanism: Disrupts outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria by displacing Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ from lipopolysaccharide (LPS) → membrane permeabilization → rapid bactericidal activity.
drugs.spectrum: MDR/XDR Gram-negative bacteria only: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella pneumoniae (KPC/MBL CRE). NOT Gram-positive, Proteus, Burkholderia (intrinsic resistance).

dose.standard: Specialist/pharmacy protocol only. Verify whether local dosing is expressed as colistin base activity (CBA) or million units (MU); systemic therapy usually requires a loading dose and ongoing PK-guided maintenance
dose.loading: Loading dose is generally required for serious systemic infection, but the exact expression (CBA vs MU) must be verified before ordering

renalAdj.regimen: Do not rely on a fixed one-line dose. Use pharmacist/ID protocol with explicit unit verification (CBA vs MU) and close renal monitoring
Highly individualized PK-guided dosing only; dialysis modality and effluent flow materially change exposure

sideEffects: Nephrotoxicity (major dose-limiting toxicity; up to 60% — monitor SCr q48h, avoid concurrent nephrotoxins)
Neurotoxicity: peripheral neuropathy, perioral paraesthesia, ataxia (may indicate toxicity — reduce dose or stop)
monitoring: SCr and urine output q48h — minimize nephrotoxic co-medications
Colistin plasma levels (target steady-state average 2–4 mg/L)
publicNotes: Colistin is generally a last-resort polymyxin for MDR gram-negative infections
It is usually paired with another active agent and requires close renal monitoring

references.text: IDSA Guidance on Resistant Gram-Negatives — Tamma et al., CID 2023

drugs.pkpd: Ward-reference summary focused on safety review, renal handling, and monitoring rather than exhaustive prescribing.
drugs.mechanism: See class-specific pharmacology; use this entry as a deterministic bedside safety reminder.

renalAdj.regimen: Review dose and interacting P-gp inhibitors

drugs.name: Dapagliflozin
